name: Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University (Nanyang MBA)

program.options: 12 months; 14 months (Singapore + Japan double degree); 24 months (double degrees with St Gallen or France)

class_size.note: class size not published on the pages read

tuition_total.stat: list price incl. 9% GST (S$85,280 before GST)
tuition_total.note: Fee schedule total S$92,955.20 incl. GST, enrolment fee payable on acceptance deducted from tuition (S$21,800 on fee schedule, S$21,600 on admissions page). Singapore citizens/PR and NTU alumni get a 10% grant; sponsored employees 15% (20% for 2+ from same organisation).

mandatory_fees_total.note: One-time miscellaneous fee S$620 incl. GST (insurance, IT, exam fees per FAQ). Application fee S$100 not included.

living_budget_total.note: FAQ: average monthly living expenses S$1,200-1,500 assuming on-campus dormitory; no total budget published.

scholarship.note: No average award or share of class published. Named awards: APEC scholarship (full tuition + S$1,350 monthly stipend + S$500 books + travel), ASEAN scholarship (S$25,000 tuition + S$1,350 monthly stipend), K.N. Sellappah (10% of tuition), many partial merit/diversity scholarships (amounts not stated), Corporate Leaders MBA Fellowship (full tuition, sponsored).

employment.note: Career Stats image on the programme page (cohort not stated): 93% employed within 3 months of graduation; 92% pivoted sector, geography or function; 'Average Alumni Salary' US$134,213 (an alumni figure, not a starting base salary, timing not stated, so not used as base_salary). Full career report is behind a HubSpot lead form (not submitted): industry, function, geography and salary splits not read. Top employers listed without hire counts (GSCDO page, all postgraduate programmes).

profile.note: Class Profile image (cohort not stated). Admission minimum: 2 years work experience, FAQ mentions GMAT > 600.

notes: NTU news (19 Feb 2026) also reports FT-sourced figures: US$194,918 average salary three years after graduation, +136% vs pre-MBA; these are FT data, cite only as one fact if needed.
